name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+12, giving Democrats a structural advantage even in a strong Republican environment
Schneider has raised $3.6M with $1.7M on hand; Lambrecht reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
No public polls or expert ratings; the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: A D+12 district, Schneider's overwhelming fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing the race near 97% Democratic all point to a safe incumbent hold, with no polls or ratings suggesting any competitive threat.
model.watch: Any polling showing a single-digit race, or a late surge of outside spending against Schneider, would be the first sign of a tighter contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider, a Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans about twelve points Democratic at the presidential level. He has raised roughly $3.6 million and holds $1.7 million on hand, while Republican Carl Lambrecht reports no fundraising figures. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets price Democratic chances near 97 percent.

The combination of a strongly Democratic electorate, an established incumbent, and a large financial edge makes Schneider a clear favorite. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the exact margin less certain than the overall outcome.
